arxiv-2011-07661.title: hyper-sinh: An Accurate and Reliable Function from Shallow to Deep Learning in TensorFlow and Keras
arxiv-2011-07661.creator: Luca Parisi, PhD, MBA Candidate luca.parisi@ieee.org
arxiv-2011-07661.description: Abstract This paper presents the ’hyper-sinh’, a variation of the m-arcsinh activation function suitable for Deep Learning (DL)-based algorithms for supervised learning, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). hyper-sinh, developed in the open source Python libraries TensorFlow and Keras , is thus described and validated as an accurate and reliable activation function for both shallow and deep neural networks.

arxiv-2011-14180.title: Approximation and localized polynomial frame on conic domains Thanks: The author is partially supported by Simons Foundation Grant #849676.
arxiv-2011-14180.creator: Yuan Xu
arxiv-2011-14180.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yuan Xu. Highly localized kernels constructed by orthogonal polynomials have been fundamental in the recent development of approximation and computational analysis on the unit sphere, unit ball, and several other regular domains. In this work, we first study homogeneous spaces that are assumed to contain highly localized kernels and establish a framework for approximation and localized tight frames in such spaces, which extends recent works on bounded regular domains.

arxiv-2111-00207.title: PatchFormer: An Efficient Point Transformer with Patch Attention
arxiv-2111-00207.creator: Cheng Zhang, Haocheng Wan, Xinyi Shen, Zizhao Wu
arxiv-2111-00207.description: Abstract The point cloud learning community witnesses a modeling shift from CNNs to Transformers, where pure Transformer architectures have achieved top accuracy on the major learning benchmarks. However, existing point Transformers are computationally expensive since they need to generate a large attention map, which has quadratic complexity (both in space and time) with respect to input size.

arxiv-2206-15408.title: Sub-8-Bit Quantization Aware Training for 8-Bit Neural Network Accelerator with On-Device Speech Recognition
arxiv-2206-15408.creator: Kai Zhen † Hieu Duy Nguyen † Raviteja Chinta ⋆ Nathan Susanj † Athanasios Mouchtaris † Tariq Afzal ⋆ Ariya Rastrow †
arxiv-2206-15408.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kai Zhen † Hieu Duy Nguyen † Raviteja Chinta ⋆ Nathan Susanj † Athanasios Mouchtaris † Tariq Afzal ⋆ Ariya Rastrow †. We present a novel sub-8-bit quantization-aware training (S8BQAT) scheme for 8-bit neural network accelerators. Our method is inspired from Lloyd-Max compression theory with practical adaptations for a feasible computational overhead during training.

arxiv-2212-12972.title: Optical mirages from spinless beams
arxiv-2212-12972.creator: Jorge Olmos-Trigo, Diego R. Abujetas, Cristina Sanz-Fernández, Aitzol García-Etxarri, Antonio García-Martín
arxiv-2212-12972.description: Abstract Spin-orbit interactions of light are ubiquitous in multiple branches of nanophotonics, including optical wave localization. In that framework, it is widely accepted that circularly polarized beams lead to spin-dependent apparent shifts of dipolar targets, commonly referred to as optical mirages.

arxiv-2307-09489.title: J. B. S. Haldane’s Rule of Succession
arxiv-2307-09489.creator: Eric–Jan Wagenmakers 1, Sandy Zabell 2, and Quentin F. Gronau 3
arxiv-2307-09489.description: Abstract After Bayes, the oldest Bayesian account of enumerative induction is given by Laplace’s so-called rule of succession : if all n n observed instances of a phenomenon to date exhibit a given character, the probability that the next instance of that phenomenon will also exhibit the character is n + 1 n + 2 \frac{n+1}{n+2} .

arxiv-2309-04589.title: Motif-aware Attribute Masking for Molecular Graph Pre-training
arxiv-2309-04589.creator: Eric Inae, Gang Liu, Meng Jiang
arxiv-2309-04589.description: Abstract Attribute reconstruction is used to predict node or edge features in the pre-training of graph neural networks. Given a large number of molecules, they learn to capture structural knowledge, which is transferable for various downstream property prediction tasks and vital in chemistry, biomedicine, and material science.

arxiv-2310-18511.title: 3DCoMPaT ++ : An improved Large-scale 3D Vision Dataset for Compositional Recognition Thanks: Corresponding authors: H. Slim and M Elhoseiny with the Department of Computer Science, KAUST, Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. E-mail: habib.slim@kaust.edu.sa; mohamed.elhoseiny@kaust.edu.sa A. Prajapati, S. Pothigar
arxiv-2310-18511.creator: Habib Slim, Xiang Li, Yuchen Li, Mahmoud Ahmed, Mohamed Ayman, Ujjwal Upadhyay
arxiv-2310-18511.description: Abstract In this work, we present 3DCoMPaT ++ , a multimodal 2D/3D dataset with 160 million rendered views of more than 10 million stylized 3D shapes carefully annotated at the part-instance level, alongside matching RGB point clouds, 3D textured meshes, depth maps, and segmentation masks.

arxiv-2409-09130.title: FAST : Boosting Uncertainty-based Test Prioritization Methods for Neural Networks via Feature Selection
arxiv-2409-09130.creator: Jialuo Chen, Jingyi Wang, Xiyue Zhang, Youcheng Sun, Marta Kwiatkowska, Jiming Chen, Peng Cheng
arxiv-2409-09130.description: Abstract . Due to the vast testing space, the increasing demand for effective and efficient testing of deep neural networks (DNNs) has led to the development of various DNN test case prioritization techniques. However, the fact that DNNs can deliver high-confidence predictions for incorrectly predicted examples, known as the over-confidence problem, causes these methods to fail to reveal high-confidence errors.

arxiv-2503-21232.title: Knowledge Graphs as World Models for Semantic Material-Aware Obstacle Handling in Autonomous Vehicles
arxiv-2503-21232.creator: Ayush Bheemaiah & Seungyong Yang
arxiv-2503-21232.description: Abstract The inability of autonomous vehicles (AVs) to infer the material properties of obstacles limits their decision-making capacity. While AVs rely on sensor systems such as cameras, LiDAR, and radar to detect obstacles, this study suggests combining sensors with a knowledge graph (KG)-based world model to improve AVs’ comprehension of physical material qualities.

arxiv-2504-11360.title: Posterior Consistency in Parametric Models via a Tighter Notion of Identifiability
arxiv-2504-11360.description: Abstract We investigate Bayesian posterior consistency in parametric density models with proper priors, challenging the common perception that the topic is settled. Classical results from the 1970s established posterior consistency as a consequence of MLE convergence, by combining regularity conditions with the assumption of model identifiability.

arxiv-2510-11785.title: Spin and Obliquity Distributions of Low-mass Planets Shaped by Dynamical Instability
arxiv-2510-11785.creator: Dieran Wang, Jiaru Li, Dong Lai
arxiv-2510-11785.description: Abstract Exoplanetary systems hosting multiple low-mass planets are thought to have experienced dynamical instability, during which planet-planet collisions and mergers occur; these collisions can impart substantial amount of angular momentum to the merger remnants, changing the obliquities of the resulting planets significantly.

arxiv-2512-21388.title: Disorder driven maximum in the magnetoresistance of spin polaron systems
arxiv-2512-21388.creator: Tanmoy Mondal 1 and Pinaki Majumdar 2
arxiv-2512-21388.description: Abstract Ferromagnetic polarons are self trapped states of an electron in a locally spin polarised environment. They occur close to the magnetic T c T_{c} in low carrier density local moment magnets when the electron-spin coupling is comparable to the hopping scale.

pmc-12985501.title: Differences in Scalp Hair Trace Element Concentrations in Patients with Preserved Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (HFpEF) Compared with Controls: A Hypothesis-Generating Study
pmc-12985501.creator: Tomasz Urbanowicz, Anetta Hanć, Zofia Kasperowicz, Oliwier Adamczak, Ievgen Spasanenko, Katarzyna Gabriel, Andrzej Tykarski, Zbigniew Krasiński, Beata Krasińska
pmc-12985501.description: Background: The pathophysiology of HFpEF is complex and characterized by systemic inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and endothelial dysfunction. Trace element involvement in redox balance, mitochondrial function, and calcium signaling is postulated. This cross-sectional analysis aimed to investigate possible differences in hair scalp trace element concentrations in patients with HFpEF and controls.

pmc-13374223.title: Enhancing the understanding of environmental microbiomes through topic modeling: a quantitative and qualitative analysis
pmc-13374223.creator: Anna S. Kujat, Christiane Hassenrück, Stefan Lüdtke, Matthias Labrenz, Theodor Sperlea
pmc-13374223.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundUnderstanding ecosystem dynamics is essential for assessing ecosystem health, yet remains challenging due to complex biotic and abiotic interactions. Microbial communities are valuable indicators of environmental change, but the high dimensionality of microbiome data requires advanced analytical methods.
